in_arabic.name: جمشید
in_arabic.meaning: منشأ الفضل والسمو، سيد المذاهب والمعتقدات
in_arabic.long_meaning: جمشید هو أسماء إسلامية مشروعة تعني "منشأ الفضل والسمو" وتعزى إلى سيد المذاهب والمعتقدات، وهو اسم يظهر في التوراة والإنجيل والقرآن الكريم. يُعتبر جمشيد أحد أشهر الأسماء اليهودية، ويُستخدم في اليهودية والديانات الإبراهيمية كإسم لمؤسس الإمبراطورية الإثيوبية في القرن الرابع عشر الميلادي، وهو ما يبرز أهمية الإسم في تاريخ الإنسانية. في الإسلام، يُعتبر جمشيد اسمًا للنبي زيد بن حارثة، ويُستخدم أيضًا في التسمية البديعة للإمام الحسن البصري. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم الإسم لتعريف الشخص ذي الفضل والسمو، ويكون مناسبًا لذوي الشخصية الممتازة والأخلاق العالية. من أهم أسباب إختيار الإسم جمشيد هو وجود الصفة الخالصة في كلماته، حيث يحتوي على الكاف واللام والسمو والفضل، مما يجعله مناسبًا للذين يرغبون في إعطاء طفلهم اسمًا يتناسب مع شخصيته المبهرة.

in_hindi.name: जमशीद
in_hindi.long_meaning: जमशीद एक पवित्र नाम है जिसका अर्थ है "विद्वान, ज्ञानी और वीर"। इस नाम का उल्लेख पवित्र ग्रंथों में किया गया है, जैसे कि पवित्र गीता, पवित्र बाइबिल और पवित्र कुरान में। यह नाम हिंदू और मुस्लिम समुदायों दोनों में उपयोग किया जाता है। इस नाम का महत्व यह है कि यह व्यक्ति के शैक्षिक और चरित्र को दर्शाता है।

In Arabic, the name Jamshed is derived from the root "J-M-Sh" and is associated with the concept of excellence and glory. In Islamic tradition, Jamshed is the name of the prophet Zaid bin Haritha, and is also used as a title for the Imam al-Hasan al-Basri. In modern times, the name Jamshed is used to signify a person of excellent character and high moral values. It is also associated with the concept of wisdom and knowledge, and is considered a fitting name for a person who embodies these qualities.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jamshed is deeply rooted in Persian and Islamic history, representing a liege lord, ruler, or king who was renowned for his justice, wisdom, generosity, and chivalry. Jamshed's tale, as recorded in various Persian, Arabic, and Indian texts, underscores the importance of a just and virtuous ruler in ensuring the peace and prosperity of his kingdom and people. Additionally, the name Jamshed has been adopted as a given name, particularly among peoples with Persian, Islamic, and Indian cultural backgrounds, reflecting the ongoing influence and continuation of this historic figure's legacy.
data.spiritual_significance: Jamshed's name can also be seen as a spiritual reflection of two essential virtues in Islamic and Persian cultures: justice and wisdom. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "There are two types of the prey (spoils of war) that Allah has forbidden for us to take: al-Khamr (intoxicants) and the fat of domestic pigs" (Muslim). Jamshed's virtuous rule is an excellent reminder of the Islamic principle of establishing justice and fairness in society, as mentioned in the Quran: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing in the way of Allah, bearing witness in equity; and let not the hatred of a peoples distract you not from justice. But be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." (Quran 5:8) Wisdom, as described in the Quran, is the ability to understand and apply divine guidance in one's life: "And indeed We have explained in this Quran for people every kind of example; and man is exceedingly ungrateful." (Quran 30:58) Jamshed's exemplary wisdom and unwavering commitment to justice serve as inspiration for us to emulate these virtues in our lives and strive towards personal and communal growth.
